name: Small Bets
tagline: Community and live classes for people building a portfolio of small online bets
summary: Daniel Vassallo left a ~$500K Amazon job in 2019 and ran several small products instead of one startup: a $25 Twitter audience course, an AWS book, and the Small Bets community with a one-time lifetime fee. Small Bets made $824,409 revenue in its first two years; he sold it to Gumroad for $3.6M in April 2025.
origin: Vassallo quit AWS in 2019 and wrote a widely shared post explaining why, which gave him his first few thousand followers. In April 2020 he recorded a 100-minute webcam course on building a Twitter audience in about 16 hours and sold it on Gumroad for $25. He launched Small Bets in November 2021 as a paid community for people following the same approach.
howItMakesMoney: One-time payments: a lifetime membership to Small Bets (live classes from members and guests, community chat, recordings), plus the earlier $25 Twitter course and an AWS book. No recurring subscription.
growth: The 'why I quit a $500K job' post drove initial attention
Shared exact revenue and hours per product publicly on X, which became marketing
The $25 Twitter course (13,000+ sales, ~$310K) proved his audience would buy
Recruited members to teach classes inside Small Bets, adding content without him producing it all
Raised the lifetime price over time, creating urgency to join early
moat: Community network effects (thousands of lifetime members and member-run classes) plus Vassallo's personal following and public track record.
risks: Lifetime pricing means no recurring revenue; income depends on continuous new members. Much of the value was tied to the founder, which the sale to Gumroad had to address.

timeline.event: Leaves Amazon Web Services job paying ~$500K to work for himself
Launches $25 'Everyone Can Build a Twitter Audience' course on Gumroad
Reports Small Bets: 500 hours for $545,072 profit; Twitter course: 16 hours for $270,971 profit
Sells Small Bets to Gumroad for $3.6M (50% cash, 50% stock), ~6,700 members

lessons: Measure each product by profit per hour invested, not MRR
A cheap, fast product (a 16-hour webcam course) can validate an audience before a larger bet
Communities scale when members teach each other, not just the founder
Transparency about numbers can be the marketing for a business-advice product
A lifetime-fee community can still be sold if membership and content are documented

rebuild.idea: A lifetime-fee community and class series for early-career public servants or NGO staff building side incomes within their employer's ethics rules
rebuild.why: Most indie-business communities assume tech workers; government and nonprofit staff face specific conflict-of-interest rules and have no dedicated space.
mvp: Write one public post about your own side income under those constraints
Run a free live session on what is and isn't allowed, collect emails
Offer a $99 lifetime founding membership with 4 scheduled live classes
Invite 2 members to teach classes on their own side projects
rebuild.fit: Someone who has worked in that sector and already runs a small permitted side project
